Data structures of the proposer and the end determination functions

This document specifies the contract that the two user supplied functions of an swfcalib job must respect:

  • make_next_proposals — the proposer: what to try next.
  • get_result — the end determination function (determ_end): is this job finished, and if so with what values.

It describes what they receive, what they must return in each situation, and shows concrete examples. The built-in factories (make_shrink_proposer(), make_proposer_se_range(), determ_poly_end(), determ_end_thresh()) are used as worked illustrations.

The running example is the one from the vignette: an HIV model with 9 calibrated parameters and 9 outcomes, n_sims = 400.

1. Where the two functions are called from

Both functions are stored in the job and are invoked from calibration_step1() (see R/calibration_steps.R), in this order, once per iteration:

calibration_step1()
  |
  |-- process_sim_results()        # merge proposals + sim outputs -> results.rds
  |-- results <- load_results()    # all iterations of the CURRENT wave
  |
  |-- update_calibration_state()
  |     |-- get_jobs_results()     # (1) job$get_result(calib_object, job, results)
  |     |                          #     -> NULL or 1-row tibble, FOR EVERY JOB
  |     |-- update_done_status()   #     wave done if no job returned NULL
  |     |-- update_default_proposal()  # write returned values into default_proposal
  |     |-- update_wave_iteration()    # iteration + 1, or wave + 1
  |
  |-- make_proposals()
        |-- job$make_next_proposals(calib_object, job, results)   # (2)
        |     ... only for jobs NOT done, and only when iteration > 1
        |-- merge_proposals() / fill_proposals() / adjust_proposal_number()

Two consequences that drive everything below:

  1. get_result always runs before make_next_proposals. A proposer may therefore rely on a sideload written by the end determination function of the same iteration (this is exactly how make_shrink_proposer() + determ_poly_end() work together).
  2. get_result is called for every job of the wave, including jobs that already converged, while make_next_proposals is called only for jobs that are not done (get_current_jobs(calib_object, not_done_only = TRUE)). See §4.5 — a converged job must keep returning its result.

Iteration numbering

moment state$iteration results contains
calibration start 0 nothing (no results.rds yet)
1st call to step 1 0 -> 1 empty tibble; get_result is not called, initial_proposals is used
2nd call to step 1 1 -> 2 iteration 1 (n_sims rows)
N-th call to step 1 N-1 -> N iterations 1 .. N-1

So, at a given call of step 1:

  • get_result sees results up to and including the iteration that just ran.
  • make_next_proposals sees the same results object, and its output is labelled with the next iteration number.

Every new wave restarts this counter at 1 (increment_wave()): results is empty again (it is read from the new wave’s directory), the sideloads are deleted, and initial_proposals is used once more. Neither function can see anything from a previous wave except through default_proposal.

2. The inputs (identical for both functions)

Both functions have the signature:

function(calib_object, job, results)

2.1 calib_object

The full calibration object (R/calib_object.R). Job functions should only touch it through accessors; in practice they use it for two things:

swfcalib::load_sideload(calib_object, job)          # read data saved earlier
swfcalib::save_sideload(calib_object, job, x)       # store data for later
swfcalib::get_default_proposal(calib_object)        # current best values, all params

Useful fields, for reference:

calib_object$config$n_sims            # 400   - simulations per iteration
calib_object$config$max_iteration     # 100   - fail-safe
calib_object$config$default_proposal  # 1-row tibble, ALL calibrated parameters
calib_object$state$wave               # 1
calib_object$state$iteration          # 3
calib_object$state$done               # FALSE - whole wave done?
calib_object$state$jobs_done          # c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE)

The sideload is a per-job, per-calibration scratch file (<root_directory>/sideloads/wave1-job1.rds). It holds anything (a list is customary). It is deleted when the wave changes (clear_sideloads()), so a sideload never survives from one wave to the next. load_sideload() returns NULL when nothing was ever saved — which is the normal state at iteration 1.

2.2 job

The job definition, plus an id injected by initialize_job_ids():

job <- list(
  id          = "wave1-job4",                       # "wave<i>-job<j>"
  targets     = c("cc.linked1m.B", "cc.linked1m.H", "cc.linked1m.W"),
  targets_val = c(0.829, 0.898, 0.881),
  params      = c("tx.init.rate_1", "tx.init.rate_2", "tx.init.rate_3"),
  initial_proposals    = <tibble, n_sims rows, one column per param>,
  make_next_proposals  = <function>,
  get_result           = <function>
)

targets[i] is paired with targets_val[i]. Nothing in the framework pairs targets[i] with params[i] — that pairing is a convention of the built-in functions (see §5.3 and §5.4), not of swfcalib itself.

2.3 results

A tibble built by merge_sim_results() — a right_join of the proposals with the simulation outputs — accumulated with bind_rows over all iterations of the current wave. It is reset to an empty tibble at each new wave.

Columns, in order:

block columns source
parameters every parameter of default_proposal — not only job$params proposals
bookkeeping .proposal_index, .wave, .iteration proposals
outcomes every column returned by the simulator — not only job$targets model

Rows: n_sims per iteration (more if the simulator returns several rows per proposal — the join keeps them all).

Example, for wave 1 at the moment get_result is called on iteration 2 (n_sims = 400, so 800 rows):

# A tibble: 800 x 21
   hiv.test.rate_1 hiv.test.rate_2 ... tx.init.rate_3 hiv.trans.scale_1 ...
             <dbl>           <dbl>              <dbl>             <dbl>
 1        0.002             0.00351           0.412               2.47
 2        0.00201           0.00587           0.187               2.47
 ...
   .proposal_index .wave .iteration cc.dx.B cc.dx.H ... i.prev.dx.W
             <int> <dbl>      <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>         <dbl>
 1               1     1          1   0.612   0.799         0.081
 2               2     1          1   0.615   0.902         0.079
 ...

Note that hiv.trans.scale_1 is constant here: it is a wave-2 parameter, so during wave 1 it is filled from default_proposal. Both functions must therefore subset explicitly with job$params / job$targets and never assume results only holds their own columns.

results can contain NA outcomes (a failed or degenerate simulation). Both functions are responsible for dropping them, e.g.:

ok <- vctrs::vec_detect_complete(results[, c(job$params, job$targets)])
results <- results[ok, ]

3. The proposer — make_next_proposals

3.1 Contract

make_next_proposals <- function(calib_object, job, results) {
  # ...
  dplyr::as_tibble(<data>)
}

It must return a tibble / data.frame with:

rule detail
columns exactly one column per name in job$params, named identically
no extra columns anything else flows into the proposals and is passed to the simulator
rows one row per parameter set to test; should be config$n_sims
types the types expected by the simulator (usually numeric)
no NA every row is going to be simulated
no bookkeeping .proposal_index, .wave, .iteration are added by swfcalib

Returning NULL, a vector, or a list is not valid — merge_proposals() calls nrow() on the output.

3.2 What happens to the returned tibble

make_proposals() post-processes every job’s output (R/proposal.R):

  1. merge_proposals() — bind_cols all jobs of the wave. Jobs returning fewer rows than the longest one are padded by resampling their own rows with replacement.
  2. fill_proposals() — columns of default_proposal absent from the proposals (parameters of other waves, or of jobs already converged) are appended with their current best value.
  3. adjust_proposal_number() — the table is resampled down to, or padded up to, exactly config$n_sims rows.
  4. .proposal_index (1:n_sims), .wave and .iteration are appended.

The practical rule: return exactly n_sims rows. Fewer means some of your proposals are duplicated at random; more means some are silently dropped.

3.3 Example — single parameter, converging

Wave 1 / job 1: params = "hiv.test.rate_1", n_sims = 400.

Iteration 1 — the proposer is not called; job$initial_proposals is used:

dplyr::tibble(hiv.test.rate_1 = seq(0.002, 0.006, length.out = 400))

Iteration 2 — make_shrink_proposer(400, shrink = 2) is called with the 400 rows of iteration 1. determ_poly_end() has just stored list(centers = 0.003904) in the sideload. The observed range of the last iteration is [0.002, 0.006], so spread = (0.006 - 0.002) / 2 / 2 = 0.001, and the new proposals span [0.002904, 0.004904]:

# A tibble: 400 x 1
   hiv.test.rate_1
             <dbl>
 1         0.00411
 2         0.00318
 3         0.00477
 ...
400         0.00352

(The values are a seq() of length 400 over the shrunk interval, sample()d so that neighbouring .proposal_index values are not correlated.)

Iteration 3 — the range of iteration 2 is [0.002904, 0.004904], the new center is 0.003851, so spread = 0.0005 and the proposals span [0.003351, 0.004351]. The interval halves at every iteration.

3.4 Example — several parameters at once

Wave 2 / job 1: params = paste0("hiv.trans.scale_", 1:3) with make_proposer_se_range(400, retain_prop = 0.3). The proposer computes the squared error over the 3 targets for every row of results, keeps the best 30 %, takes the per-parameter range of that subset, and draws a Latin Hypercube inside the resulting box:

# A tibble: 400 x 3
   hiv.trans.scale_1 hiv.trans.scale_2 hiv.trans.scale_3
               <dbl>             <dbl>             <dbl>
 1              2.31             0.394             0.352
 2              2.58             0.428             0.311
 3              2.44             0.371             0.338
 ...
400              2.49             0.410             0.327

Note the difference with make_shrink_proposer(): here the rows are a joint design over the 3 parameters (the parameters interact), whereas the shrink proposer builds each column independently.

3.5 Example — a naive custom proposer

A proposer does not have to be clever. This one is valid and self-contained:

make_random_walk_proposer <- function(n_new, sd = 0.1) {
  force(n_new); force(sd)
  function(calib_object, job, results) {
    best <- swfcalib::get_default_proposal(calib_object)[, job$params]
    out <- lapply(job$params, function(p) {
      rnorm(n_new, mean = best[[p]], sd = sd * abs(best[[p]]))
    })
    names(out) <- job$params
    dplyr::as_tibble(out)
  }
}

Output for job$params = c("a", "b") and n_new = 5:

# A tibble: 5 x 2
       a     b
   <dbl> <dbl>
1  0.982  4.21
2  1.05   3.88
3  0.941  4.09
4  1.11   3.95
5  0.996  4.30

3.6 Proposer situations summary

situation expected output
iteration 1 function not called — job$initial_proposals is used
job already converged function not called — the value from default_proposal is used for every proposal
normal iteration n_sims x length(job$params) tibble
all results rows are NA for the targets drop them first; if nothing is left, fall back to a wide/initial range rather than producing NaN
the proposer needs history store it with save_sideload(); results already holds every iteration of the wave, use .iteration to slice
the proposer cannot proceed stop() with an explicit message — this aborts step 1 and the workflow (this is what make_shrink_proposer() does when no centers sideload exists)

4. The end determination function — get_result

4.1 Contract

get_result <- function(calib_object, job, results) {
  if (<not converged>) return(NULL)
  <one-row tibble of calibrated values>
}

Exactly two valid return values:

return meaning
NULL the job is not finished — keep proposing and simulating
a one-row tibble / data.frame with one column per job$params the job is finished, and these are the calibrated values

Rules for the non-NULL case:

  • one row exactly. update_default_proposal() does default_proposal[, shared] <- result[, shared]; more than one row corrupts the default proposal (or errors).
  • column names must match job$params. Matching is done by intersect(names(result), names(default_proposal)); a misspelled name is silently ignored, and the parameter keeps its default value forever.
  • extra columns that do exist in default_proposal will be written — only return what the job owns.
  • no NA / NaN — these values become the final calibrated parameters.

4.2 Consequences of returning non-NULL

update_calibration_state() then:

  1. marks the job done in state$jobs_done (update_jobs_done_status());
  2. writes the values into state$default_proposal (update_default_proposal()), so every subsequent proposal — of this wave and of all later waves — uses them;
  3. if all jobs of the wave returned non-NULL, the wave is marked done and the calibration moves to the next wave (or finishes, writing calibrated.csv and full_results.rds in step 3).

4.3 Example — not converged

get_result(calib_object, job, results)
#> NULL

That is the whole output. Iteration continues (until config$max_iteration, at which point step 1 stop()s).

4.4 Example — converged

Single-parameter job (determ_poly_end(0.001, poly_n = 5) on hiv.test.rate_1):

# A tibble: 1 x 1
  hiv.test.rate_1
            <dbl>
1         0.00385

Multi-parameter job (determ_end_thresh(thresholds = rep(0.02, 3), n_enough = 100) on the transmission scalers):

# A tibble: 1 x 3
  hiv.trans.scale_1 hiv.trans.scale_2 hiv.trans.scale_3
              <dbl>             <dbl>             <dbl>
1              2.47             0.425             0.334

And the resulting default_proposal after the update:

# A tibble: 1 x 9
  hiv.test.rate_1 ... tx.init.rate_3 hiv.trans.scale_1 hiv.trans.scale_2 hiv.trans.scale_3
            <dbl>              <dbl>             <dbl>             <dbl>             <dbl>
1         0.00385              0.358              2.47             0.425             0.334

4.5 Important: get_result must be stable

get_jobs_results() calls get_result on all the jobs of the wave at every iteration, converged ones included, and the wave is considered done only if no job returns NULL in that same pass:

done <- !any(vapply(job_results, is.null, logical(1)))

A job that converged at iteration 4 but returns NULL at iteration 5 un-does the wave and blocks it. So a converged job must keep returning a non-NULL result on every later iteration.

This is naturally satisfied by the built-ins because results only grows:

  • determ_end_thresh() counts rows within the thresholds — that count is monotonically non-decreasing.
  • determ_poly_end() keeps predicting from an increasingly dense sample around the solution; also, once the job is done it stops proposing, so its parameter column is constant on the new rows and the prediction barely moves.

If you write a custom end function that is not naturally monotonic, make it idempotent explicitly:

get_result <- function(calib_object, job, results) {
  sl <- swfcalib::load_sideload(calib_object, job)
  if (!is.null(sl$final)) return(sl$final)     # already converged: re-emit
  # ... convergence test ...
  if (!converged) return(NULL)
  out <- dplyr::as_tibble(setNames(as.list(values), job$params))
  swfcalib::save_sideload(calib_object, job, c(sl, list(final = out)))
  out
}

4.6 get_result situations summary

situation expected output
iteration 0 (nothing simulated yet) not called at all
not enough / too noisy results NULL
converged this iteration 1-row tibble, columns = job$params
already converged in a previous iteration the same 1-row tibble again (never NULL)
partially converged (some params ok, some not) NULL — a job is all-or-nothing; split it into several jobs if the parameters are independent
it wants to hand information to the proposer save_sideload() before returning, since get_result runs first
max_iteration reached without convergence still NULL; update_wave_iteration() raises "Max iteration exceded, stopping."

5. The built-ins, end to end

5.1 make_shrink_proposer(n_new, shrink = 2) (R/proposers.R)

  • Reads load_sideload(calib_object, job)$centers, a numeric vector with one value per job$params, in the same order.
  • Errors (stop("No centers were provided for shrinkage, abort!")) when the sideload is absent — so it must be paired with an end function that writes centers, i.e. determ_poly_end().
  • For each parameter: takes the range of the last iteration only, halves it (/ shrink / 2 on each side of the center), clips the new interval to the observed range, lays n_new equally spaced points in it and shuffles them.
  • Returns an n_new x length(job$params) tibble.

5.2 make_proposer_se_range(n_new, retain_prop = 0.2) (R/proposers.R)

  • Computes sum_j (outcome_j - target_j)^2 over all iterations of the wave.
  • Keeps the best ceiling(nrow * retain_prop) rows, takes the per-parameter range of that subset, and draws lhs::randomLHS(n_new, length(job$params)) rescaled to that box.
  • Returns an n_new x length(job$params) tibble.
  • Constraint: the loop that collects the ranges iterates over seq_along(job$targets) while indexing the parameter columns, so this proposer assumes length(job$params) == length(job$targets). With fewer targets than parameters it errors; with more, the extra ranges are ignored.
  • NA outcomes propagate into the score and then into the ranges — filter them out in the simulator or wrap this factory.

5.3 determ_end_thresh(thresholds, n_enough) (R/determ_end.R)

  • Keeps the rows where abs(outcome_j - target_j) < thresholds[j] for every j (thresholds is one value per target, in job$targets order).
  • If nrow(kept) > n_enough: returns the single row of parameters whose standardized distance to the per-column median is smallest — which.min(rowSums(abs(x - median(x)) / sd(x))).
  • Otherwise returns NULL.
  • Writes no sideload, so it cannot drive make_shrink_proposer().
  • Edge case: if a retained parameter column is constant, sd(x) == 0 yields NaN and which.min() may pick an arbitrary row.

5.4 determ_poly_end(threshold, poly_n = 3) (R/determ_end.R)

  • Pools all (param_i, target_i) pairs into two long vectors, so it fits a single polynomial across all the parameters of the job. This is only valid when the parameter/outcome relationship is the same for every pair (e.g. the three race-specific tx.init.rate / cc.linked1m pairs); otherwise use one job per parameter.
  • Drops incomplete rows, standardizes, fits lm(value ~ poly(param, poly_n)), and inverts it by optimize() to get the parameter value predicted to hit each target. Those values are newp.
  • Always writes the sideload list(centers = newp) — including on the iteration where it returns NULL. That is what the shrink proposer consumes, and why the first call (no previous centers) returns NULL unconditionally.
  • Returns the 1-row tibble of newp only when both conditions hold for every target: the prediction moved less than threshold since the previous iteration, and the predicted outcome is within threshold of the target.
  • Because it overwrites centers at every iteration, the sideload always reflects the latest estimate.

5.5 Pairing summary

proposer compatible end function why
make_shrink_proposer() determ_poly_end() only needs the centers sideload
make_proposer_se_range() determ_end_thresh() (or determ_poly_end()) uses no sideload
custom any as long as the sideload contract matches

6. Checklist

Proposer (make_next_proposals)

End determination (get_result)
